RFT Number: [6000042656 (ENQ22-108)]

#### **5. INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS**

### 5.1 **Communications** 

All communications and Bidder enquiries in connection with this RFT must be sent in writing to the address set out in the Company Contact Details section of the RFT Summary in Section 4 of this RFT ("**RFT Summary**").

### 5.2 **English Language** 

All documents and correspondence relating to this RFT shall be in English language. If any documentation relating to this RFT is submitted by the Bidder in another language in addition to English, the English version shall take precedence and be used for interpreting the information.

### 5.3 **Facsimile / email not acceptable**

Submission of the Bid should be in accordance with the requirements set out in the RFT Summary. Facsimile or email submission of any Bid is not acceptable.

### 5.4 **Two-stage bidding (Technical & Commercial)**

Bidder is required to submit its Bid in the following two submissions, in closed envelopes, in accordance with the following two stage bidding process:

#### Technical Bids:

To be submitted in accordance with:

- ➢ the requirements in the Technical Bid section of the RFT Summary; and
- ➢ the requirements set out in Appendix 7 of this RFT.

The Technical Bid **must not** include any pricing information.

#### Commercial Bids:

Commercial Bids will only be invited from those Bidders whose Technical Bids are technically acceptable and compliant with the terms of this RFT.

To be submitted in accordance with:

- (i) the requirements in the Commercial Bid section of the RFT Summary; and
- (ii) the requirements set out in Appendix 8 of this RFT.

The Bidder shall submit with the Commercial Bid:

- (i) the Commercial Bid Submission Form set out in Appendix 4 of this RFT ("**Commercial Bid Submission Form**") signed by an authorized signatory of the Bidder; and
- (ii) a copy of the power of attorney evidencing the authority of such signatory to sign the Commercial Bid Submission Form on behalf of the Bidder.

### 5.5 **Bid Timetable** 

The tentative timetable for the bid process is set out in Appendix 1. Any changes in this timetable affecting the Bid Submission timeline shall be communicated to the Bidders solely through Tender Bulletins.

RFT Number: [6000042656 (ENQ22-108)]
```

### 5.6 **Bid Submission Date(s)**

The Technical Bid and Commercial Bid must be delivered to the Company on or before the submission date(s) and time(s) specified in the RFT Summary ("**Bid Submission Date(s)**").

Any Bid (or part thereof) received after the Bid Submission Date(s) may be subject to disqualification.

### 5.7 **Joint Ventures / Consortiums**

If the Bidder would like to submit its Bid as a joint venture or consortium it shall inform the Company within [seven (7)] days of receipt of the RFT.

The Bidder shall provide the following information to the Company:

- (a) the full legal names of each partner;
- (b) the legal address of each partner;
- (c) the name of the partner nominated to act as the manager of the joint venture or consortium;
- (d) the responsibilities of each partner in relation to the Scope of Work; and
- (e) a copy of the joint venture or consortium agreement with the Technical Bid, which shall state that:
  - (i) all partners shall be jointly and severally responsible for the performance of the Scope of Work; and
  - (ii) in the event that any partner ceases to be a member of a joint venture or consortium for any reason whatsoever the remaining partner(s) shall be fully responsible for the performance of the Scope of Work.

The Company shall review the Bidder's proposal to submit a Bid as a joint venture or consortium and shall decide, at the Company's discretion, whether this is acceptable to the Company. The Company shall notify the Bidder within seven (7) days of receiving its proposal whether the proposal has been accepted or rejected.

If the proposal is rejected by the Company, then the Bidder may proceed with submitting a Bid, not as part of a joint venture or consortium, within the timeframes set out in the RFT.

### 5.8 **No Bid Bond** 

No bid bond is required under this RFT.

### 5.9 **No Late Bids** 

Any Bid received by the Company shall be deemed to be the Bidder's final offer and any unsolicited bids of any kind from the same Bidder after the submission date will not be considered and may result in disqualification of the Bid.

### 6.6 **Correction Of Errors In Bids**

Arithmetic errors discovered by the Company in the Bid shall be construed and corrected by the Company in the following manner:

(i) if there is a discrepancy between the unit price and the total price that is obtained by multiplying the unit price and quantity, the unit price shall prevail and the total price shall be corrected, unless in the opinion of the Company there is an obvious misplacement of the decimal point in the unit price, in which case the total price as quoted shall govern and the unit price shall be corrected; and

RFT Number: [6000042656 (ENQ22-108)]

(ii) if there is an error in a total corresponding to the addition or subtraction of subtotals, the subtotals shall prevail and the total shall be corrected.

If the Bidder does not accept the correction of errors, their Bid may be disqualified by the Company.

### 6.7 **Qualifications / Qualification Statement**

Any submitted Bid shall be in strict conformance with the requirements set forth in this RFT. The Bidder as part of the Technical Bid shall submit the Qualification Statement in the form set out in Appendix 5 to this RFT ("**Qualification Statement**").

The Qualification Statement shall either (i) confirm the Bidder's conformity with the RFT or (ii) detail the Bidder's qualifications to this RFT.

Any qualification detailed elsewhere in the Bid shall not be considered.

Any qualification detailed in the Commercial Bid shall be disregarded and the Company may at its sole discretion disqualify the Commercial Bid.

The Company may, at its sole discretion, evaluate any qualifications detailed in the Qualification Statement in order to determine whether such qualification is acceptable or renders the Bid non-compliant.

Notwithstanding the forgoing, the Company shall not be obliged to consider any qualification and may reject any Bid that is qualified in any manner without providing a reason therefor.

If the Bidder does not submit any qualification in accordance with the terms and conditions of this RFT, the Company shall consider the Bid to be in strict compliance with the RFT requirements without any qualification.

### 6.8 **All Inclusive Prices** 

Any fees quoted in the Commercial Bid shall be all-inclusive of all costs and disbursements (excluding UAE VAT) and shall remain fixed for the term of the Agreement.

<span id="page-100-3"></span>

```text
### **1 GENERAL**

### **1.1 INTRODUCTION**

ADNOC LNG (hereinafter called COMPANY) operates three (3) gas processing Trains in Das Island to produce LNG, LPG, Paraffinic Naphtha, and Sulphur. The Das Island facilities receive the feed gas from ADNOC OFFSHORE. Trains 1 & 2 were built in 1974-1976 with production capacity of 2.9 million tons/year of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG). The 3rd LNG Train was built in 1991-1994 with an annual capacity of 3.2 million tons.

The Trains were commissioned in 1976. In year 2000, a study was undertaken (called Plant Integrity, Reliability and Recertification or PIRR) to extend the operational life of LNG Trains 1 and 2 to year 2019. Thereafter, the Operational life of Trains 1&2 was again extended to 2024 with required replacement / rejuvenation of the systems.

Majority of the process equipment, vessels and columns were replaced during the LNG Trains 1&2 Turnarounds which will have remnant life well beyond 2024.

As part of strategic requirement, ADNOC LNG launched in 2018 its Asset Longevity Program to extend the operation life of its three (3) LNG Trains year 2040. The Asset Longevity Program comprises of the following Work Streams:

### ❖ **Work Stream 1: (COMPANY Business as Normal)** [By COMPANY]

o All LNG Trains Plant maintenance, equipment replacements/ rejuvenation which can be carried out on stream or during individual one Train Turnarounds [Inspection and Replacement of Vessels, Classified Equipment, A/G Piping, Valves, Cold Box, MCHEs modification, obsolete instrument, CP system, Steam Boilers water tubes, Concrete and Steel Structures, etc.]

### ❖ **Work Stream 2: (Common Trains 1& 2 Turnaround)** [By COMPANY]

o Including Fixed TA Scope + Variable Scope [R&Rs for Piping, Pressure Vessels, Boilers, MCHE, Machinery, etc.]
```

```text
### ❖ **Work Stream 3: (LNG Trains 1 & 2 Rejuvenation Works)** [**By Rejuvenation Project**]

- o Trains 1&2 Utilities and Equipment Repairs that require common two train shutdown. **Work Stream 3** Rejuvenation Project FEED/DEFINE is developed by M/s Worley.
- ❖ **Work Stream 4: (Business Improvement Schemes/ Projects)** [By COMPANY]
  - o Upgrade Projects like Total Sulphur Reduction (TSR), LNG Trains Debottlenecking, etc.

![](_page_135_Picture_0.jpeg)

![](_page_135_Picture_1.jpeg)

Work stream 3 is the main scope of Rejuvenation Project. In addition, Total Sulphur Reduction (TSR) Project from Work Stream 4 will be included as part of Rejuvenation Project, while Work stream -2 (TA scope) and various other schemes will also be implemented during common Shutdown.

At present, total Sulphur content in the produced LNG lies in the range 4-9 mg/Nm3. Due to prevailing LNG market scenarios, COMPANY shall export LNG with an improved quality requirement (total Sulphur content in LNG shall be less than 1 mg/Nm3).

Following the detailed feasibility study outcomes, COMPANY decided to pursue UOP (Process Licensor) Option and undertake a fast-track Front End Engineering Design followed through Detail Engineering & Procurement Services of major items. The schedule shall enable the PROJECT to be implemented during the planned shutdowns for Trains 1 & 2 in 2025.

### **1.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVE**

The objective of the Project is to Repair / Rejuvenate LNG Trains 1 & 2 identified equipment, and extend the operation life till year 2040 whilst optimizing the common shutdown related work duration in order to avoid consequent production losses to the COMPANY, while maintaining the Plant reliability and availability and improving the quality of LNG through implementing TSR modifications for Trains 1&2.

### **1.3 PURPOSE OF DOCUMENT**

This document, contains only a brief EPC Scope of Work (SOW), is issued for high level understanding of the Project scope and to provide a summary of the Engineering, Procurement and Construction activities for Train 1 and 2 to be executed by EPC CONTRACTOR

EPC CONTRACTOR shall provide and execute the Project WORKS based on the requirements stipulated in this document as well as other documents provided as part of EPC Tender package.
```

### **3A-4.2 DETAILED ENGINEERING**

### **3A-4.2.1 Design Philosophy and Criteria**

The PLANT shall be designed and engineered in conformity with this document and the requirements set forth in the specifications and standards, design codes, recommended practices, safety design codes, included elsewhere in this AGREEMENT.

The requirements of Codes and Standards stated in the AGREEMENT are the minimum requirements with deviations or enhancements, subject to COMPANY's approval. Due care shall be exercised such that the PLANT affords ease of modularization, construction and expansion, COMMISSIONING and start-up, repair and maintenance, (including provision of permanent craneage and hoisting equipment) and shall be safe to operate under all conditions and for personnel to work in. Consideration shall also be given to the following in the design of SYSTEMS:

- The PROJECT is to be engineered in accordance with the PROJECT specifications and standards. Any deviations require prior COMPANY approval.
- Local environmental conditions and regulations must be strictly adhered to.
- No environmental hazards are to be created to upset the ecology of the surroundings.
- The PLANT, including all buildings and structures, as designed, shall be capable of safe and efficient operations for the entire life of PLANT, which is a minimum of 30 years.
- Special design considerations and safety measures shall be employed to avoid damage, structural damage, and failure due to the severe environmental conditions found in the area or to the quality of natural construction materials found in the United Arab Emirates.
- Equipment and material for incorporation into the WORK shall be in accordance with specifications and standards and Quality Requirements

### **3A-4.2.3.16.7 Human Factors Study**

CONTRACTOR shall conduct a Human Factors study to assess the interaction of personnel with the PLANT's SYSTEMS during normal operations and emergencies. The objective is to understand typical human responses to events and how they could affect levels of risks. CONTRACTOR shall utilize findings to influence aspects of the design and shall be used in the risk assessment. Ergonomic studies shall be carried out for Main Control Room.

Ergonomic design considerations and human factors shall be assessed to minimize the likelihood for human error for general control room operations, as well as emergency responses.

CONTRACTOR shall ensure that safe access is provided and arranged at appropriate height to facilitate production activities e.g. valve operation, pigging, routine maintenance and checks by Mechanical, Electrical and Control Engineering personnel. The design shall take into consideration the tasks to be performed.

All pressure, temperature and flow indicators shall be arranged so as to be clearly readable from permanent access decks/platforms.

Vessels or Tanks, where man access is allowed, shall have at least 2 manholes on each vessel of a minimum diameter of 24inch.

### **3A-4.2.3.16.8 Reliability/Availability Assessment**

CONTRACTOR shall carry out detailed specific assessments of various safety critical equipment items/systems to ensure adequate performance on demand will be provided.

The assessments shall include ESDs, HIPS systems/overpressure protection system and safety critical power and instrumentation systems (e.g. F&G panels).

In addition to traditional reliability/availability calculations, CONTRACTOR shall give consideration to vulnerability/survivability of personnel and plant to demonstrate performance in actual hazard events (i.e. smoke, heat, blast, shock, etc.) and this shall be incorporated into the assessment.

UKOOA Guidelines should be used in this study.

- Organize CSFs into discipline teams
- Establish risk likelihood and impact severity guidelines

- Briefing on the FRFTSU program goals, objectives, processes, and methodologies
- Implement the Program schedule

# EPC for ADNOC LNG Trains 1 & 2 Rejuvenation Project Tender Enquiry No. ENQ22-108

Annexure 3A-5 Rev. 0

#### **1.0 INTRODUCTION**

#### **1.1 Purpose**

This document provides a general specification for Optimization or Basic Studies to be used for COMPANY PROJECTS. It defines the minimum technical content, format for presentation and required actions by the CONTRACTOR as a result of the Study findings.

#### **1.2 Scope**

Optimization or Basic Studies are generally performed either at the feasibility stage or FEED stage of a PROJECT. However, this does not preclude the requirement for a Study in a later stage of the PROJECT cycle. This specification is applicable to all studies performed on behalf of COMPANY whether at the feasibility, FEED, EPC or other stages of a PROJECT.

This document defines the minimum requirements for Optimization and Basic Studies. As is often the case, any particular study may require more detailed analysis than is specified here. Compliance with these minimum specifications shall in no way relieve CONTRACTOR of his responsibility to provide an Optimization or Basic Study that is complete and of the highest Quality. CONTRACTOR shall use sound engineering judgment and shall conform to accepted industry practice in every aspect of his work.

All Optimization or Basic Studies shall be subject to COMPANY approval in terms of technical content, presentation and conclusions reached. The minimum requirements as stated in this specification shall not be relaxed unless a waiver is granted by COMPANY in writing.

#### **1.3 Document Organization**

This document is organized into four sections:

Section 1.0, this section, defines the purpose, scope and document organization of this document.

Section 2.0, General Requirements, defines the purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study and the minimum requirements for technical content.

Section 3.0, Presentation and Format, defines how the Optimization or Basic Study is to be formatted and presented to COMPANY.

Section 4.0, Document Submission Requirements defines the submission requirements for Optimization and Basic Studies.

### **2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS**

### **2.1 Purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study**

The purpose of an Optimization or Basic Study is to evaluate multiple Options with regard to the implementation of a certain requirement, evaluate the most promising of these options in detail, and to reach a valid conclusion about how to best proceed with the implementation. The Optimization or Basic Study is intended to define the direction of all subsequent engineering development. It is also intended to provide an early check on scope and Quality so that COMPANY can ensure that all requirements are being met.

Typical examples of Optimization or Basic Studies include, but are not limited to:

- Process Equipment Selection Studies
- Process Flow Scheme Optimizations
- Control System Hierarchy Studies
- Advanced Process Control Strategies
- Process Unit Layout Optimizations
- Pipeline Corrosion Protection Studies
- Pipeline/Compressor Sizing and Optimization
- Process Simulation Studies
- Construction / Modularisation Studies

#### **2.2 Minimum Technical Requirements**

- 2.2.1 For each Optimization or Basic Study, CONTRACTOR shall define the largest number of possible solutions or options practical. The actual number can be expected to vary from study to study, depending on the subject.
- 2.2.2 Each of these options shall be examined in brief detail, sufficient only to allow them to be ranked from best to worst. CONTRACTOR shall clearly define the criteria by which the options are ranked.

- 2.2.3 A minimum of the two best options shall be selected for further examination. These two best options shall be examined in detail for such parameters as cost, schedule impact, constructability, operability maintainability, safety and any other relevant contracting parameters.
- 2.2.4 When selecting and evaluating options, CONTRACTOR shall take into consideration "Proven State of the Art" technologies. Technologies that are obsolete or that will soon become obsolete shall generally be avoided. Technologies that are considered prototypes and/or are not considered "Proven" shall generally be avoided.
- 2.2.5 All drawings, contracting calculations, third-party documentation, descriptions of standard industry practice and all other data relevant to the options shall be included in the Optimization or Basic Study.
- 2.2.6 All data presented for comparison shall be normalized to the same contracting and/or currency units to allow easy and rapid comparison.
- 2.2.7 Detailed cost quotes shall be obtained from potential suppliers for all options selected for study. In addition, the cost of the options shall be evaluated both in terms of total installed cost and total lifecycle cost. All cost data shall be presented in terms of present worth using discounted cash flow calculations.
- 2.2.8 Optimization and Basic Studies shall be written in a stand-alone manner and shall contain all relevant data including life cycle cost analysis, cost benefit analysis required to independently support the conclusions.
- 2.2.9 Optimization and Basic Studies shall be written in a vendor-neutral manner wherever possible. Specific equipment may be used for the sake of example or clarity, but this shall be clearly defined. When the study itself is dealing with vendorspecific choices, this shall be clearly identified.
- 2.2.10 Optimization and Basic Studies without adequate material to independently support the conclusions shall not be accepted. CONTRACTOR shall clearly state and justify any assumptions or estimates made.

#### **3.3 Proforma Table of Contents**

Section 3.2 on the previous page illustrates a pro-forma table of contents for an Optimization or Basic Study. The following paragraphs describe each of the sections in more detail.

### **3.3.1 Executive Summary**

This section shall be written as a 1 page abstract of the study intended for mid and upper level management that are not technical specialists. It shall provide a brief overview of the study and shall include all important recommendations and conclusions.

#### **3.3.2 Introduction**

This section shall provide a complete introduction to the study as per the prototype table of contents. The purpose of this section is to tell the reader what the study is for, the limitations of the study, and how the study is organized.

#### **3.3.3 Summary of Available Options**

This section begins the study proper. It shall include the necessary PROJECT background to provide the reader with the framework to interpret the evaluation criteria and the options proposed. The purpose of this section is to rank a global sampling of options, choose the best options for further analysis and to present the evaluation criteria that will be used for all options.

Each following subsection shall present a brief description of the available options. Included in these descriptions shall be advantages and disadvantages for each available option sufficient to allow a general ranking of all options.

The summary subsection shall list the options that have been chosen for further analysis and the reasons for these choices.

#### **3.3.4 Analysis of Options**

Sections 3, 4, and 5 shall each present a detailed analysis of each option according to the stated evaluation criteria. Each of these sections shall contain sufficient data to independently support the study results. Drawings, calculations, or any other data may be directly included in the text or may be included as an attachment to the study. In any event, these documents shall be clearly referenced in the text.

### **1 GENERAL**

#### **1.1 INTRODUCTION**

ADNOC LNG (hereinafter called COMPANY) operates three (3) gas processing Trains in Das Island to produce LNG, LPG, Paraffinic Naphtha, and Sulphur. The Das Island facilities receive the feed gas from ADNOC OFFSHORE. Trains 1 & 2 were built in 1974-1976 with production capacity of 2.9 million tons/year of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG). The 3rd LNG Train was built in 1991-1994 with an annual capacity of 3.2 million tons.

The Trains were commissioned in 1976. In year 2000, a study was undertaken (called Plant Integrity, Reliability and Recertification or PIRR) to extend the operational life of LNG Trains 1 and 2 to year 2019. Thereafter, the Operational life of Trains 1&2 was again extended to 2024 with required replacement / rejuvenation of the systems.

Majority of the process equipment, vessels and columns were replaced during the LNG Trains 1&2 Turnarounds which will have remnant life well beyond 2024.

As part of strategic requirement, ADNOC LNG launched in 2018 its Asset Longevity Program to extend the operation life of its three (3) LNG Trains year 2040. The Asset Longevity Program comprises of the following Work Streams:
```

#### ❖ **Work Stream 1: (COMPANY Business as Normal)** [By COMPANY]

- o All LNG Trains Plant maintenance, equipment replacements/ rejuvenation which can be carried out on stream or during individual one Train Turnarounds [Inspection and Replacement of Vessels, Classified Equipment, A/G Piping, Valves, Cold Box, MCHEs modification, obsolete instrument, CP system, Steam Boilers water tubes, Concrete and Steel Structures, etc.]
- ❖ **Work Stream 2: (Trains 1& 2 Turnaround)** [By COMPANY]
  - o Including Fixed TA Scope + Variable Scope [R&Rs for Piping, Pressure Vessels, Boilers, MCHE, Machinery, etc.]
- ❖ **Work Stream 3: (LNG Trains 1 & 2 Rejuvenation Works)** [**By Rejuvenation Project**]
  - o Trains 1&2 Utilities and Equipment Repairs that require common two train shutdown
- ❖ **Work Stream 4: (Business Improvement Schemes/ Projects)** [By COMPANY]
  - o Upgrade Projects like Total Sulphur Reduction (TSR), LNG Trains Debottlenecking, etc.

![](_page_69_Picture_0.jpeg)

**Work Stream 3** Rejuvenation Project FEED/DEFINE is developed by M/s Worley.

Work stream 3 is the main scope of Rejuvenation Project. However, Construction package from Total Sulphur Reduction (TSR) Project will be included as part of Rejuvenation Project, while Work stream -2 (TA scope) and various other schemes will also be implemented during common Shutdown.

### **1.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVE**

The objective of the Project is to Repair / Rejuvenate LNG Trains 1 & 2 identified equipment, and extend the operation life till year 2040. Also, the Project objective is to optimize the common shutdown related work duration in order to avoid consequent production losses to the COMPANY, while maintaining the Plant reliability and availability.

The purpose of the document is to define EPC Scope of work for EPC CONTRACTOR, who shall provide and execute the Engineering, Procurement and Construction for this project. All necessary actions to comply with the above requirements are deemed included in EPC CONTRACTOR's scope.

In case of any inconsistency or discrepancy, the following order of precedence shall be followed in general. However, such discrepancies shall be brought to the attention of COMPANY and COMPANY decision shall be final.

- 2. ADNOC HSE Standards
- 3. This Document

- 4. Project Drawings and Documents
- 5. COMPANY Codes of Practice, Standards and Specifications
- 6. International codes, standards and practices

#### **1.5 CODES AND STANDARDS**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall comply (and ensure compliance of any SUBCONTRACTORs) with UAE Legislation and Environmental Regulations, applicable internationals laws & regulations, ADNOC Guidelines / Standards, project specific specifications and specifications as listed in the relevant documents, COMPANY HSE Regulations and Standards, Codes of Practice and relevant International Standards. EPC CONTRACTOR shall identify and list all the latest revisions of the applicable Codes and standards.

Contract Agreement shall remain applicable throughout the respective project / contract, unless otherwise specified by COMPANY.

Any discrepancies between latest codes and standards requirements as against design requirements defined in the SOW shall be clarified with COMPANY and shall be summarized & submitted for COMPANY Approval. COMPANY's decision shall be considered as Final. Latest COMPANY standards will be made available along with the ITT.

- Provide new pipe supports for the new chlorine lines
- De-siltation of Seawater intake basin
- Repair works at Retaining walls, CW screening area, Pumping Station and trash conveyer concrete structures

- Replace MRB critical components (Relays, Diodes and Terminal Blocks) with new ones, in SS-T1/T2/U Marshalling Relay Boxes
- Replace CW pump hydraulic discharge valves including local control panels, associated tubing and branch cables (Note: During replacement of valves, alternate sea water supply to the hypochlorite plant is required. - Replace obsolete Plant-42 band/bar screen control system with new system
- Replace control valve (CV) pneumatic positioners with smart positioners
- Utility (Instrument Air) Tie-ins of replaced CV Smart positioners
- UPS power sourcing for instrumentation at Outstations-3, 4, 5 & 7

#### **2.7 OPTIONAL SCOPE**

#### **2.7.1 LEAK DETECTION SYSTEM**

COMPANY intends to install Leak Detection System (LDS) for online monitoring of trends towards leaks in the CW and FW network. Various leak detection technologies available in the industry were evaluated as part of FEED.

EPC scope includes verification and installation of Acoustic Based External Leak Detection System for the entire CW and FW piping network.

All factors like pipe network (not pipeline), ATEX certification, installation feasibility etc. shall be considered while designing leak detection system for CW and FW pipe network.

During EPC Stage, EPC CONTRACTOR shall:

- 1. Site survey existing cooling water and fire water network along with the leak detection system vendor
- 2. Prepare detailed Specification
- 3. Obtain and review Technical and Commercial proposals for the Acoustic Emission-based LDS
- 4. Prepare Technical and Commercial Bid Evaluation Reports
- 5. Detail engineer, Inspect and ship to site, new LDS
- 6. Install leak detection system on piping network and commission the system

For detailed requirements and scope, refer Scope of Work for Acoustic Emission Based Leak Detection System for Cooling Water and Firewater Piping (WP1), Doc. No.: RJ-100-A4J-0-00352- 0001.

An interim report containing all necessary information along with native CAESAR II files shall be submitted for COMPANY's review and comments before proceeding with the final report. #### **5.7.3 BASIS OF DESIGN**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall develop Basis of design for Instruments & control systems, which shall clearly identify the basis for design of each item of instrument & control and safety systems including applicable COMPANY's standard specifications, National & International Codes & standards, critical data such as Site survey, Adequacy verification report/OEM input on the existing systems, existing system/equipment design aspects to maintain the uniformity. based on agreement with respective operating Companies/End users. Template of the document shall be agreed with COMPANY prior to development of the document.

### **5.7.4 DATASHEETS**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall prepare datasheets for all new instruments/valves which are necessary and to be installed as per the job requirement. Selection and specifications of instruments/valves shall be as per latest COMPANY specifications followed by COMPANY approval.

### **5.7.5 INSTRUMENT SIZING CALCULATIONS**

Sizing calculations shall be carried out using INSTRUCALC software complying to ISA standards for instruments such as Pressure Safety valve, Control valve, Orifice plate as applicable. Calculations performed as part of the design, are to be documented. The objective, basis, assumptions, design criteria, methodology, references must be clearly stated in the calculation sheet.

#### **5.7.6 INSTRUMENT/JB LAYOUT AND CABLE ROUTING**

- Latest as built Instrument/JB location layout drawings shall be utilized and updated for any additional or modification of existing instruments or JB locations.
- The cable routing drawing shall clearly show details of all the cables running in the routes. Any diversion, combining or change of direction of routes, road crossing, entry to building, instrument cables crossing with electrical cables, etc. shall be shown with cable routing layout details. Cable routing shall also show the branch cables from individual field Instruments as well.
- The latest instrument/JB location and cable routing layout shall be verified during site visit with current As-built conditions.

#### **5.9.4 MARINE AND SEA WATER INTAKE SCOPE**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall review the documentation prepared during FEED stage and shall develop detailed repair method statements along with pertinent supporting calculations, where required, to perform the activities related to the following:

- De-siltation of stilling basin
- Replacement of Chlorination piping
  - o Removal of existing chlorine dosing lines
  - o Removal of minimum 1m width of marine growth from the diffusers, 3m ID intake pipelines and intake risers along the route of new chlorine dosing line.
  - o Installation of new chlorine dosing lines supports
  - o Installation of new chlorine dosing lines
- Enabling works pertaining to repair activities of submerged structures located at the perimeter of stilling basin
- Isolation of chambers via installation of stop logs / dam boards to facilitate performing repair activities at screening area and pumping station of NSI structures

EPC CONTRACTOR, based on the FEED documentation, shall prepare detailed location drawings. EPC CONTRACTOR shall review the standard repair details prepared during FEED and shall update them and / or prepare defect specific repair details and repair specification along with a detailed defect register, for the scope related to the repair of Sea Water Intake Structure. EPC CONTRACTOR shall also update the existing as built drawings or develop new as-built drawings of the repaired areas.

With the exception of repair activities at screening area and pumping chambers, where works to be performed in dry conditions, all other activities are foreseen to take place via diving activities. Accordingly, EPC CONTRACTOR shall propose a qualified Diving SUBCONTRACTOR for COMPANY approval. EPC CONTRACTOR, in liaison with COMPANY shall provide site establishment, including utilities, materials, laydown areas and temporary facilities for diving operations. EPC CONTRACTOR and his Diving SUBCONTRACTOR shall adhere to COMPANY's HSE standards along with International standards. The order of precedence as stipulated in Project Documentation shall be followed.

### **7.11 FORWARDING AND LOGISTICS**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall co-ordinate the activities of shipment by land, sea or air through the vendor and as may be appropriate the freight or shipping agency/line. At all times EPC CONTRACTOR will keep the COMPANY informed on all matters concerning shipment consistent with the requirements of customs, insurance, shipping, practices, and the requirements of the schedule.

#### **7.12 PRESERVATION & LONG-TERM STORAGE**

#### **7.12.1 PRESERVATION**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall ensure that packaging and preservation of equipment, items, instruments, etc. at the vendor's /EPC CONTRACTOR's works / store are as per contract requirement. Any vendor recommendations for storage and preservation of vendor supplied material at site shall be ensured by EPC CONTRACTOR.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall prepare detailed preservation procedures and submit for COMPANY approval prior to starting the work (procedures shall cover re-testing of systems and equipment at store / site). If any of the facilities are intended to be unused for long term as per the SOW, the same needs to be preserved by EPC CONTRACTOR as per COMPANY guidelines.

#### **7.12.2 LONG TERM STORAGE**

This requirement shall be deemed necessary only if the storage requirement is in excess of 12 months.

![](_page_211_Picture_0.jpeg)

![](_page_211_Picture_1.jpeg)

All packages should be stored indoor in a dry environment or may be stored outside. Where packages are stored outside then they must be raised off the ground (minimum of 4" / 10 cm) and covered with tarpaulin or other suitable heavy-duty waterproof membrane. The tarpaulin must be adequately secured to prevent ingress of moisture and regularly checked, especially during high winds.

### **7.13 ON SITE INSTALLATION AND INTEGRATION**

Where the contract / purchase order requires on worksites (e.g.: site assembly of equipment) for the system, EPC CONTRACTOR will keep COMPANY informed on all matters concerning shipment consistent with the requirements of customs, insurance, shipping, practices and the requirements of the schedule.

It is the EPC CONTRACTOR's responsibility to ensure that all activities & plans required for installation / transportation of equipment material to the site is carried out in a safe manner.

#### **8.3 SIMULTANEOUS OPERATIONS (SIMOPS)**

Simultaneous Operation (SIMOPS) will occur continuously with construction activities. SIMOPS Procedures will therefore be required to be followed for the safe integration of production activities with construction activities.

WORK activities must be carefully planned and executed such that one activity does not adversely affect another activity. If it is anticipated that activities being considered cannot satisfy this fundamental criterion, task rescheduling is the preferred course of action. Where tasks cannot be rescheduled and Simultaneous Operations (SIMOPS) are necessary, the potential increased risk of conducting work activities simultaneously and in close proximity must be understood and ultimately reduced to a level that is As Low as Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) as agreed by COMPANY designated SIMOPS authorities.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall note that SIMOPS was carried out during FEED and the same shall be reviewed and updated as required to capture detailed design development / construction activities.
```

EPC CONTRACTOR's scope of work for piping erection includes, but shall not be limited to:

- 1. All dimension verifications prior and during erection.
- 2. All erection, testing and re-instating of the piping systems, including supporting.
- 3. All bolt tensioning required according to the pipe specifications otherwise to be provided by EPC CONTRACTOR for COMPANY approval.
- 4. Supply, installation and dismantling of temporary supports
- 5. Installation of cleaning screens, filters, etc.
- 6. All other necessary activities such as marking, re-stamping, inspection, documenting, establishing procedures, obtaining approval from COMPANY, etc.
- 7. Surface protection, priming, painting, touch-ups, etc.

#### **8.13.2 WELDING**

EPC CONTRACTOR's SCOPE OF WORK for welding includes for, but shall not be limited to:

- 1. Preparation and qualification of welding procedures
- 2. Qualification of welders
- 3. Supply of test weld materials
- 4. Submission of all procedures and qualifications to COMPANY for approval.
- 5. Execution of all welding in accordance with the approved procedures and QA/QC requirements.
- 6. Maintain a welding control system documentation agreed by COMPANY.

![](_page_246_Picture_0.jpeg)

![](_page_246_Picture_1.jpeg)

#### **8.13.3 HEAT TREATMENT**

EPC CONTRACTOR's scope of work shall include pre and post weld heat treatment, where type of material, material thickness, design code of specifications required to do so. The scope of heat treatment includes the preparation of detailed procedures for COMPANY approval.

### **8.13.4 NON-DESTRUCTIVE TESTING (NDT)**

EPC CONTRACTOR's scope of work for non-destructive testing includes for, but shall not be limited to:

- 1. Application of test methods such as:
  - a. Radiography (X-ray & Gamma ray)
  - b. Ultrasonic examination
  - c. Dye penetrate testing
  - d. Hardness testing
  - e. Magnetic particle examination
  - f. Advanced NDT technique for Baseline Inspection, with prior approval from COMPANY.
- 2. Preparation of a detailed procedure for COMPANY approval.
- 3. Maintaining a complete weld tracking system per group of piping specifications.
- 4. Provision of third-party inspection (TPI).
- 5. All tie-in joints are to be hydro tested using joint testers and mechanical seal plugs.

#### **8.13.5 HYDROTESTING, FLUSHING, DRAINING & PURGING**

EPC CONTRACTOR's scope of work for hydro testing, flushing, draining, drying and purging includes for, but shall not be limited to:

- 1. Preparation of hydro-test
- 2. Preparation of procedure for hydro testing / pneumatic testing including definition and extent of last sections for COMPANY approval.
- 3. Preparation of all necessary testing equipment such as certified/calibrated pressure gauges, dead weight tester, hoses, air compressors, dummy spools for instrumentation, calibration facilities, recorders for logging of the hydro test/pneumatic test, temporary gaskets and flanges, etc.

#### **Handling, Hauling, Storage and Transportation**

EPC CONTRACTOR shall load and transport the material, equipment's and structural parts using suitable means to avoid damages from manufacturer's yard to the Work site. A pre-load meeting shall be held prior to commencing load out operations. At this stage all material shall be checked to ensure that it is undamaged. It is EPC CONTRACTOR responsibility to provide the supervision, equipment and consumable items for all on board material loading activities.

Before loading of material, commences satisfactory completion of all necessary testing and acceptance vessel shall be met.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall submit to COMPANY for approval a detailed procedure for storage, handling and transportation of Piping, electrical, instrumentation material and equipment. The procedures shall include, but not be limited to, details on loading, unloading, storage area, modes of transportation, method of material handling and various equipment's to be used. This shall also include necessary drawings of cargo barges for handling, hauling, storage, traceability and transportation prior to commencement of any handling operations.

Loading, transporting, and unloading shall be performed in such manner as to prevent damage to material, their respective coatings. If transported material coating and equipment sustain damage, EPC CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for all repair and/or replacement costs.

EPC CONTRACTOR shall carry out a dynamic transportation analysis based on storm conditions mentioned elsewhere in the contract, considering the proposed marine transportation scheme i.e. cargo barges and the securing arrangement and establish that the proposed transportation arrangement is safer and stable. The results of the analysis shall be submitted to COMPANY for approval, prior to undertaking the transportation of material to the works site(s).
